summary: Core Media I/O is the API for publishing custom camera devices as system extensions (providers, devices, streams, clients, properties) and for the legacy DAL plug-in model. BifrOSt has a Linux V4L2 capture path inside the system layer that the Camera app uses, but no SDK API for apps to read cameras, and nothing that publishes a camera device to other apps.

features.feature: Providers (extension provider and its source and properties)
features.apple: CMIOExtensionProvider, CMIOExtensionProviderSource, CMIOExtensionProviderProperties; article: Creating a camera extension with Core Media I/O
features.note: No mechanism lets an app or service publish a virtual camera to other apps. No SDK module and no loopback device wiring found (no v4l2loopback reference in the tree).
probe() enumerates /dev/video* nodes and keeps only single-planar capture devices with streaming (usable()). Discovery only; there is no device-side publishing.
mmap streaming with VIDIOC_* ioctls; converts YUYV, NV12, NV21 and MJPEG to RGBA. Consumed only by the Camera app inside the shell, not exposed as a stream API.

features.apple: CMIOExtensionClient; system-enforced camera access through system extensions
features.note: The Camera app opens the device only while it is on screen and releases it on stop, and shows Camera not available when no node works. There is no client identity or permission check for other apps. The app sandbox in springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs grants /dev/snd and /dev/dri but no /dev/video node.

features.apple: Apple's Camera app and AVFoundation consumers of these devices (no Core Media I/O symbol)
features.note: Viewfinder, self-timer, grid, front/back switch, JPEG capture and QR scan. Single built-in app, no SDK for other apps.

features.feature: Properties (property, state, attributes, info and mach service keys)
features.note: V4L2 capability flags are read internally. No property model or extension info dictionary exists for app developers.

features.apple: Overriding the default USB video class extension (DriverKit driver matching)
features.note: Driver matching for UVC devices is the Linux kernel's uvcvideo driver. BifrOSt does not override it, and the DriverKit model has no Linux counterpart.

features.apple: Device Abstraction Layer (DAL) Plug-Ins: structures, functions, enumerations, data types, errors. Apple recommends replacing them with Core Media I/O extensions.
features.note: DAL is an Apple-only legacy plug-in model. No counterpart on Linux.

gaps: No SDK API for apps to enumerate cameras or open a capture stream; the V4L2 path in springboard/src/media/v4l2.rs is reachable only from the shell's Camera app.
No way for an app or service to publish a virtual camera device to other apps (no loopback or provider model).
The app sandbox (springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs) does not grant /dev/video nodes to apps, so a sandboxed app cannot open a camera even with an SDK API.
No per-client access prompt or permission model for camera use by apps (Core Media I/O clients are system-enforced).
Camera property model (controls, attributes, state) is not exposed to apps.
